historical_record.description: The house then on the lot went up around 1899.

Having sustained a negative declaration for a seven-unit apartment building on the site a week earlier, the City Planning Commission voted 6-0 to hold the case for 30 days, ask the developer not to demolish the old building, and have the Landmarks Board study its history.

After five months' delay while neighbours sought a buyer to save the shingled house on the lot, the City Planning Commission unanimously approved the permit for an apartment building in its place, keeping the front palm tree; the Landmarks Board had found the house did not qualify as a landmark (Resolution 7676).
